transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what really got me to come in is this thing that happens when I start eating sometimes. It’s not just, like, “oh I had too much” or I wanted a snack or whatever. It’s more like once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some kind of switch, and then I just keep going.

And the weird part is I’m not totally unaware of it. Like, part of me is sitting there thinking, “Dennis, just stop already. You don’t even need more.” But I still keep doing it anyway, and that’s been kind of freaking me out, honestly. It feels like I’m not really in control in those moments, and that’s… yeah, that’s basically why I’m here.
After these episodes where you feel like you're not in control while eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to try to balance it out?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve definitely felt really uncomfortable afterward, like physically and mentally, and I’ll sit there thinking I shouldn’t have done that, but I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that.

And laxatives—no, that’s not something I use. Exercise… I mean, I’ll sometimes think, like, “I should do something to make up for this,” but I don’t go out and do some huge workout right after or punish myself with it. It’s more just feeling bad about it than doing something to counteract it, if that makes sense.
Do these episodes where you feel out of control while eating cause you significant distress, or affect your daily life like work, relationships, or how you see yourself?

Yeah… it does bother me, definitely. I don’t know if I’d say it’s, like, completely wrecking my life or anything, because I’m still getting to class and I still go to robotics and do the stuff I’m supposed to do most of the time.

But it kind of follows me around afterward. Like the next morning I’ll feel sort of sluggish, and it’s harder to focus, and I’ll be sitting in class thinking about what happened instead of paying attention. And with my roommates, I get really in my head about it—like, did they hear me, did they notice food missing, are they thinking something about me? I’ll spend way too much time worrying about that.

So… it hasn’t knocked me totally off track, I guess, but it messes with how I feel about myself more than I want to admit. It’s more distressing than it is, like, practically disabling, if that makes sense.

When these episodes happen, do they feel like a distinct period where you're completely focused on eating, and then it ends, or does it feel more like a gradual build-up and fade-out without a clear start or stop?

Yeah, I think it feels more like a… kind of a distinct thing, but I don’t always notice the exact second it starts, if that makes sense. Like, it’s usually on nights after I’ve had some project deadline or I’m already tired and kind of mentally fried, or if there’s leftover pizza in the apartment and it’s just there.

I’ll go in thinking I’m just going to have, like, a normal amount. But then once I start, it turns into me taking the food back to my room and eating way more than I meant to. Like, I’ve had nights where I end up eating a whole small pizza, and then chips, and then cereal too. And that’s not, like, a normal dinner amount for me or for my roommates. It’s definitely more than I planned.

So I guess there’s a build-up in the sense that the day or the stress kind of sets it up, but the actual eating part feels like this separate stretch of time where I’m just focused on eating until it’s suddenly over and I realize how much I had.
Can you describe exactly what it feels like in those moments when you realize you’ve eaten way more than you meant to? Do you feel like you were completely unable to stop yourself once you started?

Yeah… that’s actually the part that made me feel like I needed to talk to someone, because it’s not just, like, “Oh, I ate too much and now I’m full.” It feels different than that.

It’s like once I start eating that way, something kind of flips. I’ll be aware, at least partly, that I’m going past what I meant to eat. Like I’ll have this thought in my head—“Dennis, stop. You don’t even need more. You’re going to feel awful after this.” But then I still keep going. And it’s not like I’m enjoying it the whole time, exactly. At first maybe there’s relief or it feels good to just not think, but then pretty quickly it becomes this weird automatic thing where I’m still reaching for more even while another part of me is telling me not to.

So… I don’t know if I’d say I’m literally completely unable to stop, because I guess technically I could stand up and walk away. But in the moment it really doesn’t feel that way. It feels like the “stop” part of my brain is way quieter than the part that’s just like, keep eating, keep going. And then afterward I sort of snap out of it and realize how much I had, and that’s when it hits me.
Can you tell me if during these episodes you feel like you’ve lost control over your eating, like you’re not able to stop yourself even though you want to?

Yeah… yes. That’s honestly the main thing that made me think, okay, this isn’t just me having bad willpower or being hungry or something.

Because once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some kind of switch. I’ll already be thinking, like, Dennis, stop. You don’t need more. Just put it away. And I can hear that thought pretty clearly, but it’s like it doesn’t actually control what I’m doing. I just keep going anyway, even though part of me wants to stop and knows I’m going to feel bad about it after.

So I guess I wouldn’t say I black out or anything, but it feels like I lose control in the moment. Like I’m watching myself keep eating and not really being able to interrupt it.
After these episodes, do you ever fast, use diuretics, or make drastic changes to your eating or exercise routine to make up for what you ate?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I haven’t really been tracking it that specifically.

I don’t think there’s, like, a planned routine afterward where I’m clearly trying to “make up” for it. Sometimes I’ll have the thought that I should be more careful the next day, or that I should get back to normal, but I don’t know if that counts as a drastic change. It’s more like a guilty thought than a specific plan, if that makes sense.

And with diuretics, I’m not even totally sure what would count there, but nothing is coming to mind. I guess the honest answer is I haven’t noticed a consistent thing like that after the episodes.
Do you feel significant distress or concern about your body shape or weight, especially in relation to these eating episodes?

I’m… not totally sure how to separate that out, honestly.

I mean, I do feel bad after it happens, and part of that is definitely about my body, like worrying what this is doing to me or feeling uncomfortable with how I look or how I feel in my clothes. But I don’t know if I’d say it’s only about shape or weight, if that makes sense. A lot of it is more this shame or concern that I couldn’t stop, and then my mind kind of goes to, “Well, if you keep doing this, what’s going to happen to your body?”

So yes, there is concern there, but I’m not sure how significant it is compared to the other part of feeling upset about the eating itself. It’s kind of tangled together for me.
Can you describe exactly how much control you feel you have once you start eating during these episodes? Like, is there a moment where it feels like you can’t stop, even if you want to?

Yeah, there is definitely a point where it feels like I can’t stop, even if I want to. That’s kind of the part that scared me enough to come in, honestly.

It’s not like I start out thinking, “I’m going to lose control now.” At first it can feel like I’m just eating, or maybe eating more than I meant to, but then it’s like something shifts. I keep describing it like a switch because that’s really how it feels. Once I’ve crossed that line, I’m still aware of what I’m doing, but I don’t feel like I’m in charge of it in the normal way.

I’ll be thinking to myself, like, Dennis, come on, stop already. Put it away. You don’t even want this anymore. And that thought is there, it’s not like I don’t know what’s happening, but it doesn’t seem to make my hands stop or make me walk away. I just keep going.

So I guess the amount of control feels really low once it gets going. Beforehand maybe I have more choice, but once I’m in it, it feels like I’m arguing with myself and the eating side wins.

Can you tell me if these episodes have a clear beginning and end, where you can say, 'This is when it started' and 'This is when it stopped,' or does it feel more like a longer, ongoing pattern of eating without clear boundaries?

Yeah, I think there usually is kind of a beginning, at least in the ones I’m thinking of. It’s not like I’m grazing all day with no lines around it. It’s more like… there are certain nights where it turns into something.

Like after I’ve had a project deadline, especially if I’ve been stressed and then it’s finally over, or if there’s leftover pizza in the apartment, that’s when it can start. I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have a couple slices or something normal, but then I end up taking it back to my room, and it keeps going from there.

A specific example would be eating a whole small pizza, and then also chips, and then cereal after that. And at that point it’s way more than I meant to eat, and honestly way more than what my roommates would probably eat for a normal dinner. So I can kind of look back and say, “Okay, it started when I went for the pizza,” or when I decided to keep eating after I’d already had enough.

The ending is maybe less clean, but it usually stops when the food is gone or I feel too full or sort of snap out of it. So yeah, I’d say there are episodes with a start and stop, not just one long ongoing eating pattern.
Do you find yourself eating these larger amounts of food in secret because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah… I do. That’s actually one of the parts that makes me feel really embarrassed talking about it.

If my roommates are around, like if we’re all in the kitchen or someone’s making food at the same time, I’ll usually try to make it look normal. I’ll eat what seems like a normal-ish amount in front of them, like a regular dinner or a snack that wouldn’t stand out. I’m very aware of what it looks like, which sounds kind of ridiculous saying out loud, but I’ll be thinking, “Okay, this seems fine, no one would think anything weird.”

But then later, if they leave or if I can get back into the kitchen without it being obvious, I’ll take more. Or I’ll grab extra stuff and bring it back to my room, like I’m trying to avoid anyone seeing the full amount altogether. It’s not always some dramatic sneaking around, but it is secretive in that I don’t want them to see how much I’m actually eating.

And I think the reason is definitely embarrassment. I don’t want someone walking in and seeing the pile of food or noticing that I already ate and now I’m getting more. I worry they’d judge me, or even just ask, “Are you still hungry?” and then I’d have to explain it, and I really don’t want to. So yeah, I tend to hide the bigger part of it.
Can you tell me how often these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say this has occurred in the past few months?

Yeah… I’ve tried to think about that because I know “sometimes” is kind of vague. Since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually it’s one night in a week where it gets like that, where it’s clearly not just a normal amount of eating.

There are some weeks where it’s more like twice, especially if I have deadlines stacked up or if there’s a lot of food in the apartment, like leftovers or snacks just sitting around. Then it’s easier for it to happen again before I’ve really gotten back on track, I guess.

So if I had to put a number on it, I’d say usually once a week, sometimes two times in a week. And that’s been pretty steady for… probably the last three or four months at least. It’s not like it happened once or twice and then stopped. It’s been enough that I started noticing the pattern and feeling like, okay, this is becoming a thing.

So I can kind of look back and say, “Okay, it started when I went for the pizza,” or when I decided to keep eating after I’d already had enough.

The ending is maybe less clean, but it usually stops when the food is gone or I feel too full or sort of snap out of it. So yeah, I’d say there are episodes with a start and stop, not just one long ongoing eating pattern.

inference.note: The patient's description continues to support the presence of a loss of control during eating episodes, with a distinct beginning and some awareness of the behavior, but an inability to stop. There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise, which makes bulimia nervosa (F50.2) less likely. Binge eating disorder (F50.81) remains the most consistent diagnosis based on the clinical picture. However, the differential remains open due to the patient's uncertainty regarding body image concerns and the need for further clarification.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences eating episodes in secrecy due to embarrassment, which would support loss of control and distress related to binge eating.
doctor.question: Do you find yourself eating these larger amounts of food in secret because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

target_item.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
target_item.manifestation: I’ll eat a normal-ish amount if my roommates are in the kitchen, then take extra stuff back to my room later because I don’t want them seeing how much I’m actually eating.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether I eat larger amounts in secret due to embarrassment about how much I am eating.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I do. That’s actually one of the parts that makes me feel really embarrassed talking about it.

If my roommates are around, like if we’re all in the kitchen or someone’s making food at the same time, I’ll usually try to make it look normal. I’ll eat what seems like a normal-ish amount in front of them, like a regular dinner or a snack that wouldn’t stand out. I’m very aware of what it looks like, which sounds kind of ridiculous saying out loud, but I’ll be thinking, “Okay, this seems fine, no one would think anything weird.”

But then later, if they leave or if I can get back into the kitchen without it being obvious, I’ll take more. Or I’ll grab extra stuff and bring it back to my room, like I’m trying to avoid anyone seeing the full amount altogether. It’s not always some dramatic sneaking around, but it is secretive in that I don’t want them to see how much I’m actually eating.

And I think the reason is definitely embarrassment. I don’t want someone walking in and seeing the pile of food or noticing that I already ate and now I’m getting more. I worry they’d judge me, or even just ask, “Are you still hungry?” and then I’d have to explain it, and I really don’t want to. So yeah, I tend to hide the bigger part of it.

doctor.intent: Determine the frequency of the eating episodes, which is necessary to differentiate between Binge-Eating Disorder (F50.81) and Eating Disorder Not Otherwise Specified (F50.2).
doctor.question: Can you tell me how often these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say this has occurred in the past few months?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks, usually one night and sometimes two when deadlines or apartment food pile up. I’d say that pattern has been steady for at least the last three or four months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how often the binge-eating episodes have occurred over the past few months, which directly matches the frequency and duration requirement.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I’ve tried to think about that because I know “sometimes” is kind of vague. Since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually it’s one night in a week where it gets like that, where it’s clearly not just a normal amount of eating.

There are some weeks where it’s more like twice, especially if I have deadlines stacked up or if there’s a lot of food in the apartment, like leftovers or snacks just sitting around. Then it’s easier for it to happen again before I’ve really gotten back on track, I guess.

So if I had to put a number on it, I’d say usually once a week, sometimes two times in a week. And that’s been pretty steady for… probably the last three or four months at least. It’s not like it happened once or twice and then stopped. It’s been enough that I started noticing the pattern and feeling like, okay, this is becoming a thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by eating an amount of food that is definitely larger than most people would eat in a similar time period under similar circumstances and a sense of lack of control over eating during the episode. There is no evidence of compensatory behaviors (e.g., purging, fasting, excessive exercise), and the episodes cause significant distress. These features align with binge-eating disorder (BED) rather than bulimia nervosa, which requires compensatory behaviors.
